name: Strahan
note: Town: the regional hub of West Coast Tasmania on Macquarie Harbour, base for Gordon River cruises, the railway and Ocean Beach; it has its own waterfront and streetscape.

name: Ocean Beach
note: Beach: a 40 km surf beach of large dunes north-west of Strahan, reached by road from the town.

name: Hogarth Falls
note: Waterfall: a 30-minute rainforest walk from People's Park at the north end of Strahan Harbour.

name: People's Park
note: Park: forest and botanical gardens at the north end of Strahan Harbour, with picnic and camping facilities and the start of the Hogarth Falls walk.

name: Water Tower Hill Lookout
note: Viewpoint: a lookout above Strahan with views over the town and Macquarie Harbour.

name: Cape Sorell Lighthouse
note: Lighthouse: an 1899 lighthouse 40 m high on the coast near Strahan and the Macquarie Harbour entrance.

name: Sarah Island
note: Historic site: former convict penal station (1822) in Macquarie Harbour, with ruins still visible; reached by cruise from Strahan.

name: Strahan Wharf Centre
note: Museum: a display on the story of West Coast Tasmania at the Strahan wharf.

name: The Ship That Never Was
note: Live theatre performance: a play about the escape from Sarah Island, staged at the Strahan Visitors Centre; a recurring show.

name: Macquarie Harbour Cruises
note: Tour operator: cruises across Macquarie Harbour and up the lower Gordon River, from Strahan.

name: Gordon River Cruises
note: Tour operator: six-hour cruise from Strahan to the Gordon River and Hells Gates; the operator is the ride, the Gordon River is the place.

name: Gordon River
note: River: the Gordon River, cutting into Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park; visited by river cruise from Strahan.

name: Hells Gates
note: Headland: the dangerous entrance to Macquarie Harbour, passed on Gordon River cruises.

name: West Coast Wilderness Railway
note: Heritage railway: a rebuilt rail journey between Queenstown and Strahan, operated as a tour; the ride is the attraction, its ends are towns already listed.

name: Wilderness Woodworks Strahan
note: Craft shop and workshop: woodworkers make objects from salvaged Huon pine on The Esplanade, Strahan; a shop, not an attraction.

name: Wilderness Air
note: Operator: scenic flights and adventure charters from Strahan.

name: Wild River Jet Rides
note: Operator: jet boat rides on the rivers near Strahan.

name: Franklin River Nature Trail
coordinates_source: osm way highway=path 'Franklin River Nature Trail' (way centre, approximate midpoint; confirm with resolve-pin)
note: Walk: an easy 1 km rainforest trail beside the Franklin River on the Lyell Highway near Derwent Bridge.

name: Nelson Falls
note: Waterfall: a roughly 30 m fall on the Nelson River, reached by a short boardwalk trail on the Lyell Highway; a Great Short Walk.

name: Donaghys Hill Lookout
note: Viewpoint: a 30-40 minute return walk to a wilderness lookout over the Franklin River Valley, on the Lyell Highway.

name: Frenchmans Cap Track
note: Multi-day walk: a challenging 3-5 day hike to the summit of Frenchmans Cap, a dominant peak of the Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers area.

name: Lake Rhona Trail
note: Walk: a 7-10 hour (14 km) one-way track to Lake Rhona in the Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park.

name: Kutikina Cave
note: Archaeological cave: a rich Aboriginal occupation site in the Franklin River gorge; public access is likely restricted, to be checked.

name: Franklin River
note: River: the Franklin River in the Tasmanian Wilderness World Heritage Area, known for guided multi-day rafting expeditions.

name: Franklin River Rafting
note: Tour operator: guided 8-9 day Franklin River rafting expeditions, departing from Hobart.

name: King River
note: River: whitewater rafting on the King River near Queenstown, where Huon and King Billy pines grow along the banks.

name: Lake Margaret
note: Historic site: a hydropower ghost town on Lake Margaret, reached by a guided tour from the West Coast.

name: Lake Burbury
note: Lake: a reservoir beside the Lyell Highway east of Gormanston, known for trout fishing and rowboats at a luxe retreat.

name: Lake St Clair
note: Lake: Australia's deepest freshwater lake at the southern end of Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park, with the Overland Track's end and a visitor centre.

name: Cynthia Bay
note: Visitor hub: the Lake St Clair Visitor Centre and ferry departure point at the lake's southern end.

name: Lake St Clair Ferry
note: Ferry: passenger ferry from Cynthia Bay to Narcissus Bay on Lake St Clair, described as Australia's highest-altitude ferry; a vehicle, the place is the bay.

name: Echo Point
note: Viewpoint: a Great Short Walk lookout over Lake St Clair from the southern end of the lake.

name: Mount Rufus
note: Mountain walk: a Great Short Walk (3-7 hours) to the summit, with views over Lake St Clair.

name: Shadow Lake
note: Walk: an alpine lake walk near Lake St Clair, a Great Short Walk of 3-7 hours.

name: Aboriginal Cultural Heritage Walk (Lake St Clair)
note: Walk: a short guided-interpretation walk from Lake St Clair to Aboriginal sites, caves and rock shelters.

name: Overland Track
note: Multi-day walk: Tasmania's best-known walk, about 65 km from Cradle Mountain to Lake St Clair; this entry is the walk, pinned mid-route, and its southern end lies in this region.

name: Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park
wiki: Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park
coordinates_source: wikipedia:Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park
note: National park: Tasmania's most renowned park, mostly in the north-west; only its southern Lake St Clair end lies in this region, so the park is listed where most of it lies, for the region judge to confirm.

name: Mount Ossa
coordinates_source: osm node natural=peak 'Mount Ossa' (replaces Wikipedia rounded point)
note: Mountain: Tasmania's highest peak at 1,617 m, climbed by a track from Pelion Gap, inside Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park.

name: Derwent Bridge
note: Village: a small Lyell Highway village at the junction for Lake St Clair, with a hotel and the Wall in the Wilderness.

name: The Wall in the Wilderness
note: Carved timber installation: a roughly 100 m wall of carved Huon pine panels at Derwent Bridge, telling the region's history, with a self-guided visit.

name: Lyell Highway
note: Scenic road: the Lyell Highway (A10) between Hobart, Derwent Bridge and Queenstown, a drive journey past buttongrass plains; a route, not a place.

name: Iron Blow Lookout
note: Viewpoint: a lookout over the mined Iron Blow hill above Queenstown.

name: Spion Kopf Lookout
note: Viewpoint: a lookout over Queenstown and its rare rock-based football oval.

name: Queenstown
note: Town: a former mining town in a bowl of mined hills on the Lyell Highway, with a historic main street and mine tours.

name: Evans Old Corner Store & Market
note: Heritage building and market: a restored 19th-century store, with monthly markets; the building is a shop, the markets are periodic.

name: The Galley Museum
note: Museum: displays on the history of Queenstown and district, with photographs and a minerals collection.

name: Bradshaw's Sawmill
note: Working sawmill: visitors can see a working sawmill cutting Huon pine, blackwood and sassafras timber on Lynchford Road.

name: Douggie's Mine Tours
note: Tour operator: underground tours of a working copper mine near Queenstown, driven 7 km down the main decline; the operator is the tour, the mine is the place.

name: Roamwild Tours
note: Tour operator: small-group day trips from Queenstown, including a Lost Mines and Ancient Pines tour.

name: Zeehan
note: Town: a one-main-street former silver-mining town with many surviving civic buildings and a heritage streetscape.

name: West Coast Heritage Centre
note: Museum: a small history museum on Main Street, Zeehan, about life in West Coast Tasmania in the early 20th century.

name: Gaiety Grand Theatre
note: Historic theatre: a historic Zeehan theatre building; whether it is open to visitors is unconfirmed.

name: Spray Tunnel
note: Historic tunnel: a tunnel on Fowler Street, Zeehan, from its mining history.

name: Rosebery
note: Town: a mining town on the Murchison Highway, the survivor of the West Coast mining communities, base for Montezuma Falls.

name: Montezuma Falls
note: Waterfall: Tasmania's highest waterfall at over 104 m, reached by an 11.5 km return trail with a grade 2 difficulty.

name: Stitt Falls
note: Waterfall: a 30-minute rainforest walk from Stitt Park near Rosebery.

name: Rosebery Folk Festival
note: Festival: an annual folk festival in Rosebery; an event, not a permanent place.

name: Rosebery Aerial Ore Bucket Ropeway
note: Industrial relic: the old Hercules to Rosebery aerial ore bucket ropeway and a disused ore bucketway crossing the Murchison Highway.

name: Tullah
note: Town: a hydro town on the Murchison Highway between Lakes Rosebery and Mackintosh, base for the dam and steam railway.

name: Mackintosh Dam
note: Hydro dam: a hydroelectric dam with views over Lake Mackintosh, a good photo stop 4 km from Tullah.

name: Wee Georgie Wood Steam Railway
note: Miniature steam railway: a historic steam locomotive railway at Tullah, running weekends October to April; a ride with a loop, not a destination.

name: Lake Mackintosh
note: Lake: a hydro reservoir seen from Mackintosh Dam near Tullah.

name: Southwest National Park
note: National park: Tasmania's largest park in the wild south-west, part of the Tasmanian Wilderness World Heritage Area, reached by road to Strathgordon and Scotts Peak or by air and trail.

name: Strathgordon
note: Village: a hydro-electric settlement built for the dam, on the road into Southwest National Park.

name: Gordon Dam
note: Hydro dam: the Gordon Dam at Strathgordon, a large hydro-electric dam with a visitor view.

name: Knob Hill Lookout
note: Viewpoint: a lookout on Gordon River Road near Strathgordon.

name: Gordon River Road
note: Scenic road: the Gordon River Road into Southwest National Park, with spectacular views; a route, not a place.

name: Eliza Plateau
note: Plateau: a plateau in Southwest National Park, named in the park's Wikivoyage guide with no detail.

name: Red Knoll Lookout
note: Viewpoint: a small lookout at the end of C607 Scotts Peak Road over Lake Pedder.

name: Lake Pedder
note: Lake: a lake inside Southwest National Park, with Lake Pedder Lodge on its shore and access by road and boat.

name: Melaleuca
note: Remote settlement: an airstrip-only settlement in Southwest National Park, the start of many hiking trails, with the Deny King museum.

name: Port Davey
note: Fjord: one of Australia's two fjords on the wild south-west coast, reached by boat tour from Melaleuca.

name: South Coast Track
note: Multi-day walk: an 85 km trail along Tasmania's south coast, usually six to eight days one way, between Melaleuca and Cockle Creek.

name: Cockle Creek
note: Settlement: a small coastal settlement at the south end of the South Coast Track, the best access to the park's south coast.

name: Maydena
note: Small town: just outside Southwest National Park, a good base to start exploring the park.

name: South-East Mutton Bird Islet
note: Islet: one of the eight Mutton Bird Islands off the Port Davey coast, part of an Important Bird Area; boat access only, little visitor infrastructure.

name: Whale Lookout
note: Viewpoint: a coastal lookout at Recherche with a whale statue, on the Fishers Point Track.

name: Arthur-Pieman Conservation Area
note: Conservation area: 1,030 km2 of wild Tarkine coast from the Arthur River to the Pieman River, with dunes, beaches and shack communities; reached by car.

name: Edge of the World
note: Coastal viewpoint: the Edge of the World at the Arthur River mouth, the reason many travellers visit the conservation area.

name: Arthur River
note: Small town: a village at the Arthur River mouth with the Arthur River Field Centre visitor centre and a boat ramp.

name: Balfour
note: Ghost town: a deserted former copper-mining town just outside the conservation area.

name: Sandy Cape Beach
note: Beach: the conservation area's largest beach, cold and windy, reached by the Sandy Cape Track.

name: Sandy Cape Track
note: Drive track: a 48 km return 4WD track from Temma to Sandy Cape; needs an Arthur-Pieman recreational driver pass.

name: Temma
note: Shack community: a coastal shack community and beach access in the conservation area, on the Sandy Cape Track.

name: Sarah Anne Rocks
note: Coastal shack community: a shack community and beach access on the Arthur-Pieman coast.

name: Couta Rocks
note: Coastal shack community: a shack community and beach access on the Arthur-Pieman coast.

name: Bluff Hill Point
note: Coastal shack community: a shack community and headland access on the Arthur-Pieman coast.

name: Nelson Bay (Tasmania)
note: Coastal shack community: a shack community and beach access in the conservation area.

name: Corinna
note: Small settlement: a historic Pieman River settlement and the southern gateway to the Tarkine coast, with the Corinna car ferry.

name: Corinna Car Ferry
note: Vehicle ferry: an on-demand vehicle barge across the Pieman River at Corinna; a vehicle crossing, not a place.

name: Takayna / Tarkine
note: Wilderness region: the Tarkine, the largest cool-temperate rainforest in Australia, mostly in north-west Tasmania; its south end is the Arthur-Pieman coast.

name: Tasmanian Wilderness World Heritage Area
note: World Heritage area: the region-wide wilderness that contains most of the west and south-west parks; a designation, not a place to go.

name: Mount Tyndall
note: Mountain: a 1,179 m peak in the western highlands with a Wikipedia article; named by no visitor source, only an OpenStreetMap and Wikipedia entry.

name: Mount Geikie
note: Mountain: a 1,193 m peak in the western highlands with a Wikipedia article; named by no visitor source.

name: Mount Sedgwick
note: Mountain: a 1,146 m peak in the western highlands with a Wikipedia article; named by no visitor source.
